added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own baseline_suite (5d35145df, completed, 1 failure: tests/test_schema.py::test_well_formed_evidence_record_with_resolving_shas_is_quiet) and after_suite (4ae1a9613, completed, 0 failures); added ids = after_ids - base_ids = empty. The base failure is a non-git-scratch-tree artifact, not a revision defect, but it does not affect the subtraction.

findings.text: blocking: _tree_entries returns the cached Resource set whenever the directory-level signature matches, but the signature is only each directory's mtime_ns and HTML entry count, and a document rewritten in place leaves both unchanged; because resolve_resource matches on the cached resource.slug (reckon/resources.py:640) and the reuse never re-invokes identify_resource, an in-place change to a document's plan-slug or reckon-type is never seen. Reproduced: after rewriting one plan file's plan-slug meta in place, resolve_resource(new-slug) returned None and resolve_resource(old-slug) returned the file, while a fresh scan gave the opposite (reviewer-logs/inplace-identity-staleness.log). The docstring at reckon/resources.py:476-478 claims the file memo re-parses such a file, but the memo is only consulted inside identify_resource, which the reuse bypasses. The change also widens reuse from an explicit 'with resource_scan_scope()' block to a process-wide cache with no expiry, so a long-lived process (the MCP server, the producer) serves stale identity until a file is added, removed or moved in that tree. This breaks the done-when's requirement that the bounded read give the same answer as the full read.

follow-on: the base arm's single reported failure, tests/test_schema.py::test_well_formed_evidence_record_with_resolving_shas_is_quiet, is a subprocess.CalledProcessError from 'git -C /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/.../base-arm rev-parse HEAD' returning exit 128, because the base arm ran in a non-git scratch tree; the same test passes at base in a real git worktree (reviewer-logs/base-schema-test-in-git-worktree.log). The manifest's failure_attribution { } and its statement that the failure 'reproduces at the base revision' mischaracterize a base-arm environment artifact as a revision defect; added_failure_count is unaffected because the head arm has no failures.

follow-on: the head-arm log header reads '# rev: 5d35145dfb2bc3f85c598b8730df0131b86a9dd1' (the base) although the run is the head arm, so the log misnames the revision it measured; head-arm-suite.log:4 names 4ae1a9613 correctly, and the arms also collected 2145/2147 tests where a fresh collection of the same ten files in either tree yields 2149, an unexplained difference.

item_verdicts.done_when: the plan's done-when asks that the metadata index reuse a digest-keyed cache for files whose bytes are unchanged and that 'the bounded read gives the same answer as the full read on a synthetic repository'; tests/test_a_promotion_walks_the_docs_tree_once.py:112 pins the scan count and :130/:141/:152 assert the duplicate, archived and added-file guarantees, which I re-ran at head (4 passed, EXIT=0).
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to bound the promotion's plan-metadata read, reusing one docs-tree scan per unchanged tree instead of reopening and re-parsing the corpus once per slug; reckon/resources.py:531 (_tree_entries) returns the classified set while a directory signature matches, and reckon/resources.py:546 (iter_resources) applies the archived/legacy filters to it.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the node gate 4 passed EXIT=0, a base and head arm of the ten pre-existing resource-touching test files at -n 8 (base 2144 passed / 1 failed / EXIT=1, head 2147 passed / 0 failed / EXIT=0), a negative control 2 failed EXIT=1, a warm reprofile (resolve_resource 19.22 s / 8 calls vs 20.33 s / 8; fresh _scan_tree 8 to 3), and the fragment; its baseline_suite/after_suite fields both completed.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares reckon/resources.py, reckon/_store.py, the new test module and the evidence fragment/figures; git diff --name-status 5d35145df 73e10feac changes exactly reckon/resources.py (M), tests/test_a_promotion_walks_the_docs_tree_once.py (A) and the fragment (A), so the diff stays inside the fence.

justifications.durability: the declared mutation (RECKON_TEST_DROP_TREE_REUSE=1, tests/test_a_promotion_walks_the_docs_tree_once.py:52) reddens test_one_promotion_scans_each_tree_once and test_archived_plan_resolves_through_the_archive_fallback, so the reuse guard fires, but no test covers an in-place identity change, so the regression class that breaks the equivalence guarantee is unguarded.
justifications.evidence: the node gate and the negative control reproduce under my re-run (4 passed EXIT=0; 2 failed EXIT=1, logs/negative-control.log) and added_failure_count derives to 0, but the base arm's single 'failure' is an artifact of its non-git scratch tree and the head-arm log names the base revision.
justifications.fit: the cache sits beside the existing _SCAN_SCOPE idiom with a threading.Lock and a frozen dataclass sentinel (reckon/resources.py:448-463), but the docstring at reckon/resources.py:476-478 claims a rewritten document 'is re-parsed by the file memo', which the reuse path does not do.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the reuse and its speedup land and the added-file, duplicate and archived guarantees hold (reckon/resources.py:552-568), but the reused answer diverges from a full scan when an in-place content edit changes a document's identity, so the node's own equivalence done-when is not met.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-status 5d35145df 73e10feac lists only reckon/resources.py, tests/test_a_promotion_walks_the_docs_tree_once.py and the fragment, all inside the declared paths, with reckon/_store.py and the figures directory untouched.
